content.text:
**Common ground first.** All programmes below accept the same phenomenology: a component that is cold or nearly cold, dissipationless, gravitationally clustering, ~5× the baryon density (Planck 2018 CMB results, *A&A* 2020), and spatially separable from baryons in cluster collisions (Clowe et al., "A direct empirical proof of the existence of dark matter," *ApJ* 2006). What is contested is the *identity* of that component — or whether the inference is an artefact of using the wrong gravity law.

---

**1. Weak-scale WIMPs (thermal relics, ~5 GeV–100 TeV).**
The most mature programme and the one being squeezed hardest. LZ's 4.2 tonne-year analysis (LZ Collaboration, *Phys. Rev. Lett.*, published July 2025) found nothing and set the world's best spin-independent limits, of order 10⁻⁴⁸ cm² near 40 GeV; LZ subsequently pushed below 9 GeV for the first time and reported detection of solar neutrinos from ⁸B (LZ/LLNL and SURF releases, December 2025). XENONnT has now accumulated ~6.8 tonne-years and reports coherent elastic neutrino–nucleus scattering from solar ⁸B — i.e. the experiments have literally entered the "neutrino fog" that will eventually floor nuclear-recoil searches (XENON Collaboration, IDM 2026, Zaragoza; their light-dark-matter-in-the-neutrino-fog paper was a PRL Selection of the Year, announced February 2026). Complementary channels are also null: LHC has excluded coloured superpartners into the TeV range, and Fermi-LAT dwarf-galaxy limits (Ackermann et al., *PRL* 2015) cut below the canonical thermal cross-section for masses under ~100 GeV, while the Galactic-centre gamma-ray excess is well explained by millisecond pulsars (Bartels et al., *PRL* 2016; Macias et al., *Nature Astronomy* 2018). Next steps: LZ to >1000 live days by 2028, then XLZD/DARWIN and PandaX-xT.

**2. QCD axions and axion-like particles (neV–meV).**
Motivated independently of cosmology by the strong-CP problem. ADMX has reached DFSZ-model sensitivity in narrow windows around 2.7–4.2 µeV (ADMX Collaboration, *PRL* 127, 261803, 2021, and follow-ups), and a broad ecosystem — HAYSTAC, CAPP/IBS, ORGAN, QUAX, GrAHal, dielectric haloscopes (MADMAX), DMRadio and ABRACADABRA-type LC searches at lower mass, CASPEr for nuclear-spin couplings — is scanning outward. A January 2026 *CERN Courier* review ("In pursuit of the post-inflation axion") describes MADMAX as on track to reach DFSZ/KSVZ sensitivity across 40–400 µeV, the mass range favoured if the axion field is born after inflation, aided by travelling-wave parametric amplifiers and single-photon detection. No exclusion of the paradigm exists — only of slices of parameter space.

**3. Light/sub-GeV dark sectors (MeV–GeV, hidden mediators).**
The main successor to the WIMP: thermal relics too light to have appeared in xenon detectors, coupled through dark photons or scalars. Sharp, falsifiable relic-abundance targets are being attacked from two sides — skipper-CCD and cryogenic single-charge detectors (SENSEI, DAMIC-M, SuperCDMS SNOLAB) and accelerator searches (NA64, Belle II, BDX, the proposed LDMX). Substantial parameter space remains unprobed but reachable this decade.

**4. Self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) and other "CDM-plus" variants.**
Not a candidate so much as a modification: strong dark-sector self-scattering to explain the diversity of galaxy rotation curves, cluster core/density outliers, and unexpectedly compact strong-lens perturbers (see Tulin & Yu, *Physics Reports* 2018, for the framework). It is astrophysics-driven and actively simulated — including new work on SIDM cores and collapse reported in early 2026 — but its signatures remain degenerate with baryonic feedback, which is the standing objection.

**5. Ultralight/wave ("fuzzy") dark matter (10⁻²²–10⁻¹⁸ eV).**
The original selling point — kpc-scale de Broglie wavelength smoothing galaxy cusps — is essentially dead: Lyman-α forest data (Rogers & Peiris, *PRL* 2021) and dynamical heating of ultra-faint dwarfs (Dalal & Kravtsov, *ApJ* 2022) require masses orders of magnitude above 10⁻²² eV. Ultralight ALPs remain viable as dark matter at higher masses, where they behave like ordinary CDM and merge into programme 2.

**6. keV sterile neutrinos / warm dark matter.**
Its flagship signal is gone: the 3.5 keV line is inconsistent with Milky Way blank-sky X-ray data (Dessert, Rodd & Safdi, *Science* 2020), reinforced by NuSTAR analyses. Structure-formation bounds also bite — thermal-relic masses below roughly 6 keV are excluded by Milky Way satellite counts (Nadler et al., *PRL* 2021) and by combined lensing + satellites + Lyman-α analyses (Enzi et al., *MNRAS* 2021). The νMSM survives at small mixing angles, where it is very hard to test.

**7. Primordial black holes / macroscopic dark matter.**
Attractive because it needs no new particle, only non-standard early-universe physics. Microlensing (OGLE; Subaru HSC toward M31, Niikura et al., *Nature Astronomy* 2019), CMB accretion and evaporation limits leave essentially one window for 100% of the dark matter, the "asteroid-mass" range ~10¹⁷–10²³ g; LIGO/Virgo mergers do not require a PBH-dominated population. Recent reviews (e.g. "Primordial black holes: constraints, potential evidence and prospects," arXiv:2601.06024, 2026) argue for suggestive but not decisive hints, and new probes keep arriving — e.g. FRB microlensing constraints on halo-dressed PBHs (arXiv:2607.17338, July 2026).

**8. Modified gravity / no dark matter (MOND and descendants).**
Strongest where it was designed to work: the radial-acceleration relation and baryonic Tully–Fisher relation in galaxies are tight and predicted. Relativistic versions can now fit CMB and matter power spectra (Skordis & Złośnik, *PRL* 127, 161302, 2021), but generally at the cost of extra fields that behave dust-like — i.e. dark matter by another name — and cluster lensing and colliding clusters remain awkward. The much-publicised wide-binary test is unresolved: Chae reports a low-acceleration anomaly resembling MOND, Banik et al. report Newtonian consistency using the same Gaia data (both *MNRAS*, 2023–2024).

**9. The "nightmare" residual: gravitationally coupled relics.** FIMPs, superheavy WIMPzillas, gravitinos, Planck-scale remnants. Fully consistent with all data and nearly untestable except through cosmology.

---

**Ranking, best to worst current shape**

1. **QCD axion** — independent theoretical motivation, no data against it, and experiments have just begun reaching realistic couplings across broad mass ranges.
2. **Light/sub-GeV dark sectors** — well-defined relic targets, large unexplored space, and a fast-growing experimental programme with cheap, diverse detectors.
3. **WIMPs** — still the best-instrumented and most-tested hypothesis, and not excluded, but the prior has shrunk badly: two decades of null results, LHC silence, and the neutrino fog now setting a hard horizon.
4. **SIDM / CDM-plus** — healthy because it is driven by real astrophysical tensions and testable with lensing and dwarf-galaxy data, but degeneracy with baryonic physics keeps it inconclusive.
5. **Primordial black holes** — one open mass window and no new particle needed, but the window is narrow, requires tuned inflationary physics, and is hard to probe further.
6. **Ultralight/fuzzy DM** — the specific motivating regime is excluded; what survives is indistinguishable from CDM and folds into the axion programme.
7. **keV sterile neutrinos** — the anomaly that drove it has been retracted by better data, and structure formation plus X-ray limits leave only a hard-to-test corner.
8. **Modified gravity** — impressive galaxy-scale regularities, but no single theory yet matches galaxies, clusters, lensing and the CMB without smuggling in dark components, and its sharpest new test is contested.
9. **Gravitationally coupled relics** — not refuted, but almost unfalsifiable, so it cannot be in "good shape" as a research programme.

*Caveat:* my verification of very recent developments is uneven — the 2026 items above (XENONnT's combined CEvNS/light-WIMP analysis, MADMAX progress, PBH reviews) are anchored in sources I checked, but there may be mid-2026 results I have not seen, particularly from LZ, PandaX and the Korean and dielectric haloscopes.
